opening.label: Opening
opening.title: The common opening
opening.intro: A useful default. These are separate branches, not a single uninterrupted research line.

steps.title: Convalescence
steps.note: Replenishment +3% and growth +10: useful from the first repeated battles.

steps.title: Hooked Axe Blades
steps.note: Adds melee defence to the human screen, including Warriors and Akshina.

steps.title: Oblast Scavenger
steps.note: More post-battle loot; prerequisite for the movement and Akshina upgrade.

steps.title: Troll Country Pathfinder
steps.note: Movement for armies plus speed and range for Akshina. Useful for all three expeditions.

steps.title: Cold Storage
steps.note: Extra replenishment everywhere; its additional growth is specific to Frozen climates.

steps.title: Ice Cade Collars
steps.note: Weapon strength for Things in the Woods and Snow Leopards, not all forest creatures.

details: Change order for an actual reason

Move Ice Cade Collars earlier with several Things or Snow Leopards. Move a newly available unique technology forward when it improves the units already doing the fighting. Skip completed entries rather than researching them twice.
Legacy research tokens

The earlier Ostankya field guide's research tokens — ice, pathfinder, scavenger, siege, cold, collars, charms, undergrowth, shadows, glacial, dogma, convalescence and hooked — map onto the named technologies in these queues; twelve of them appear as steps above with their checked names. The “ice” token names no technology in the archive's own lookup, so an old “ice” tick must be re-read against the live tree rather than assumed to migrate. Research facts are shared across all routes, so a checked technology stays checked when you change the strategy tab.

forest.label: Witchcraft
forest.title: Grow the forest’s power
forest.intro: Unlock the crafting improvement while strengthening the roster it supports.

steps.title: Charms Above the Door
steps.note: Scouting, item drops and spell resistance. Start the unique branch when the live conditions allow it.

steps.title: Sympathetic Undergrowth
steps.note: Akshina gain Snipe; stronger movement control and army speed. Snipe is not verified extra Smart AR value.

steps.title: Fighting Shadows
steps.note: Armour for Things and forest animals. Do not assign that armour bonus to every human or Incarnate.

steps.title: Double, Double
steps.note: Adds a secondary trinket slot in the Witch’s Hut: a meaningful crafting milestone.

steps.title: Howling in the Woods
steps.note: Things gain useful missile protection and their eligible attacks can discourage enemies.

steps.title: Poacher’s Bane
steps.note: Forest spotting and additional armour-piercing damage for Incarnate Elementals.

details: The three-parent gate matters
Double, Double follows Charms Above the Door, Sympathetic Undergrowth and Fighting Shadows. It is a trinket-slot upgrade, not a sixth campaign Hex. Script and resource conditions still apply.
Empowered Hexes are a separate decision

Inspect the specific empowerment research for the Hex you actually use. Prefer mobility for a distant expedition, cleansing for plague/corruption pressure, or the final ritual’s next requirement. Do not buy every research node simply to try to advance an Essence-spending objective.

expedition.label: Expedition
expedition.title: Sustain the journey
expedition.intro: Priorities for repeated distant battles and a growing roster of veteran characters.

steps.title: Cold Storage
steps.note: Extra replenishment everywhere; its additional growth is specific to Frozen climates.

steps.title: Troll Country Pathfinder
steps.note: Movement for armies plus speed and range for Akshina. Useful for all three expeditions.

steps.title: Oblast Tactics
steps.note: Ambush success for the campaign; its anti-infantry bonus is for Dervishes and Horse Archers, not Akshina.

steps.title: Lens Crafters
steps.note: More campaign visibility; prerequisite for the recruit-rank technology.

steps.title: Gospodar Bloodline
steps.note: Additional lord and hero recruit rank; useful before establishing another experienced expedition.

steps.title: Glacial Prism
steps.note: Additional army Winds reserve; Ice Guard ammunition is relevant only when those units are fielded.

details: No blind research detours
Do not take a long chain solely because its name sounds thematic. Inspect its path, total time, cost and scope. A safe army with a modest income can continue while expensive research waits.

later.label: Later
later.title: Match your next investment
later.intro: Useful late pivots, not a mandatory shopping list.

steps.title: Aggressive Cultivation
steps.note: Melee attack for Incarnate Elementals, Frost Wyrms and Elemental Bears. Not a bonus for every feral beast.

steps.title: Ur-Stones
steps.note: Reduces upkeep of Incarnates, Frost Wyrms and Elemental Bears. Pursue when several are actually recruited.

steps.title: Siege Mentality
steps.note: Extra ammunition; its melee-defence and reload bonuses apply during siege defence.

steps.title: Devotional Creed
steps.note: Reduces plague spread and hostile Slaaneshi unit-seduction budget. Also opens Norse Hatred.

steps.title: Norse Hatred
steps.note: Combat and psychology support against the named Chaos cultures. Not a bonus against all Dark Elves or Undead.

steps.title: Formalised Dogma
steps.note: Patriarch capacity and recruit rank. Only pay for this when Patriarch access and an actual use exist.

details: Economy is also about costs avoided

Replenishment, movement and targeted monster upkeep can matter as much as a small income modifier. Build your actual recurring income first, then take a long economic branch when enough settlements will benefit.
Optional city-roster detour

After normal Kislev recruitment is genuinely unlocked, inspect the techs whose unit lists match Tzar Guard, War Bear Riders and Little Grom. Leave horse-cavalry or Ice Court capacity nodes until you intend to use those units.
